title: Stable Baseline SDK Selective Integration - port manifest
method: STATIC git archaeology only. No build, no injection, no runtime test on the analysis machine (no MSVC/ninja/g++, EXE and CMakeCache not local).

policy.portRule: Only SDK changes with explicit 1.21.120.0 evidence, clear value, and independent verifiability.
policy.separateEvaluation: MinecraftGame virtual-call guard vs ExceptionHandler context capture must never be grouped
policy.noWholesaleCherryPick: Mixed SDK+non-SDK commits: only reviewed hunks are eligible
policy.mergeToMain: FORBIDDEN this round; integration branch only

baselineFacts.note: b32d185 has only a file-local usableOffset(int) in MinecraftGame.cpp (returns offset>0 && offset<0x8000). Its DEFINE_INDEX_FIELD macro writes the raw scan result straight into a static int with no plausibility gate.
baselineFacts.playUiState: INERT: MinecraftGame_playUi uses operand 3 producing 3238145; playUi() rejects it with 'index < 2 || index >= 4096', so no virtual call is made.

thisRoundHeuristic.caveat: Loose lexical heuristic (nearby if / nullptr / && pattern). Some direct chained dereferences such as 'getBlockSource()->getBlock(...)' were counted as guarded because an unrelated check appeared in the window. It is an UPPER BOUND on guarded sites, NOT a proof of safety.

getBlockSourceConsumers.conclusion: No proof that all actually-reachable consumers handle nullptr. Porting the nullptr-return behaviour is forbidden by the 3.7 spec.

introduces: rejectOffset() / entryStatus() / usableOffset() as global gates
dependencyRoot.relationship: All four are ANCESTORS of 517646e (verified with git merge-base --is-ancestor). 517646e^:OffsetProvider.hpp already contains ResolveStatus::Missing, rejectOffset and #include <SDK/ResolveState.hpp>; b32d185 contains none of them.
dependencyRoot.consequence: Batch-1/2/3 mapping hunks are NOT independently portable to b32d185. Porting them alone either fails to apply (context mismatch) or silently degrades 'UNVERIFIED stays rejected' into 'raw garbage value used as a live offset', which is exactly the 'do not disguise UNVERIFIED as OK' failure mode.

candidates.name: Batch-1 MinecraftGame_playUi operand 3 -> 10 (slot 164)
candidates.evidence: 1.21.120 hit 0x1CBC3E4 -> disp32 0x520 -> slot 164; 1.21.44 hit 0x003DF624 -> 0x4C0 -> slot 152. Unique, 8-byte aligned, in range.
candidates.reason: b32d185 keeps playUi inert via the index>=4096 guard. Applying this hunk would ACTIVATE a real slot-164 virtual call on a baseline that has NO MemUtils::isValidVirtualCall guard. This is precisely the playUi AV investigated in 3.6.2-D/E and is explicitly forbidden by 'slot 164 must not be blindly changed'.

candidates.name: Batch-1 five IMPLAUSIBLE offsets retired as UNVERIFIED
candidates.evidence: Each hunk documents the 1.21.120 hit address and why the old operand read garbage; signatures are re-anchored to produce zero hits (honest MISSING).
candidates.reason: The 'stay rejected / consumers gate on usableOffset()' semantics require ResolveStatus + rejectOffset. On b32d185's raw macro these become either scan failures or live garbage offsets. Porting would DISGUISE UNVERIFIED as usable, which the spec forbids.

candidates.name: Batch-2 complete candidate evidence (docs + analyzer)
candidates.evidence: Full candidate lists with instruction context for 1.21.120 and reference 1.21.44.
candidates.reason: Evidence documents are non-runtime assets. They are valuable as the evidence base for any future S1 attempt, but are not SDK behaviour and must not be counted as ported functionality.

candidates.name: Batch-2 five ambiguous offsets (3 STATIC VERIFIED, 2 UNVERIFIED)
candidates.evidence: ClientInstance_getBlockSource slot 318 wrapper, GameSession_mEventCallback 0x50, Actor_mDestroying, BlockSource_setBlock slot 34; two declarations explicitly kept UNVERIFIED.
candidates.reason: Same state-machine dependency as Batch-1. In particular ClientInstance_getBlockSource's new slot-318 pattern is coupled to 9229523's plausibility gate; porting the mapping without the gate changes which object consumers receive. The two UNVERIFIED declarations would lose their rejection semantics.

candidates.name: Batch-3 BlockSource_mBuildHeight from 1.21.120 vtable getter
candidates.evidence: BlockSource RTTI .?AVBlockSource@@ -> vtable RVA 0x921B490 (66 slots); slot 38 is 'movzx eax,word ptr [rcx+0x38]; ret'; unique hit 0x5D3B130 -> 0x38; 1.21.44 corroboration only.
candidates.reason: The single hunk is a pure signature replacement and technically compiles on b32d185's old macro, but its own comment declares 'New status OK; STATIC VERIFIED', which is state-machine terminology. Its only consumer value is BlockESP, and the spec says BlockESP capability must not be built/validated until S3 consumer null-safety is complete. Net value without the state machine is low while risk is non-zero.

candidates.name: ClientInstance::getBlockSource plausibility gate -> nullptr
candidates.evidence: Offline 3.9.20.300505 analysis: ClientInstance initialiser 0x1945160 nulls 0xF0/0x108/0x110/0x118; 541 qword stores to [reg+0x118], zero fed by BlockSource vtable installer; 73 constructor calls build BlockSource on the stack, never as a heap member.
candidates.reason: Spec explicitly forbids porting the nullptr-return behaviour until all actually-reachable consumers are proven null-safe. b32d185 has 57 call sites in 21 files with direct chained dereferences such as 'getBlockSource()->getBlock(...)'. Returning nullptr would convert a wild vtable jump into an immediate null dereference across many modules (Regen, BlockUtils, BlockESP, Nuker, OreMiner, ...).
dependencies: consumer null-guard audit of all 57 call sites
or runtime proof those paths are unreachable under the test config
candidates.unblockCondition: A per-callsite null-guard patch for all reachable consumers, reviewed and built as its own batch, OR a runtime config proof that no consumer executes.

candidates.name: MinecraftSim probe retry after a failed attempt
candidates.evidence: Behavioural, not an offset: the Simulation pointer pair appears only after the world is created, later than the first getSimTimer() caller (LevelInfo / Nametags on the first rendered frame).
candidates.verdict: PORT (APPLIED as its own stage commit)
candidates.reason: b32d185:MinecraftSim.cpp is byte-identical to 411fa4e^:MinecraftSim.cpp (verified with git diff --quiet), so the hunk applies cleanly with zero context drift. It touches only one SDK file, has no dependency on ResolveState/MemUtils/GUI/GL/ESP/Aura, and the spec explicitly authorises it as an independent batch.

concurrencyReview.lock: std::mutex sProbeMutex held for the whole resolveGameSimOffset body; all shared state is accessed under it
concurrencyReview.backoff: kProbeRetryMs = 2000 via GetTickCount64(); sLastProbeTick is std::atomic<unsigned long long> with relaxed ordering
concurrencyReview.failureHandling: cached -1 is final ONLY inside the backoff window; after 2000 ms the probe runs again -> satisfies 'must not cache -1 permanently after first failure'
concurrencyReview.successHandling: cached >= 0 is returned permanently (a located offset cannot become wrong while the object lives)
concurrencyReview.logFloodGuard: sLayoutDumped (plain bool, only touched under sProbeMutex) makes the layout dump one-shot
concurrencyReview.initialisationTiming: first caller may be the first rendered frame before the world exists; deferred retry is the intended fix
concurrencyReview.renderSim: sRenderSimOffset is stored alongside sGameSimOffset on both success and failure, so resolveRenderSimOffset follows the same retry window

candidates.name: MinecraftGame::playUi MemUtils::isValidVirtualCall guard
candidates.evidence: Defensive check against a wrong-version/stale object; no 1.21.120-specific mapping evidence.
candidates.reason: b32d185 has no MemUtils::isValidVirtualCall (nor isReadableRange/isPatchableCode in the required form); porting requires dragging in MemUtils.cpp/.hpp from the state-machine batch. More importantly b32d185's playUi is already INERT (rejected by index>=4096), so the guard adds zero value on this baseline. It would only become relevant if the Batch-1 playUi mapping were also ported, which is excluded.

candidates.name: ExceptionHandler raw fault-context capture
candidates.evidence: Pure crash diagnostics (ExceptionAddress / AccessType / FaultAddress / registers).
candidates.reason: Diagnostics, NOT SDK functionality. Spec requires the virtual-call guard and ExceptionHandler context capture to be evaluated separately, and 3.7 explicitly says not to auto-port extra diagnostics onto the stable baseline. Adding crash-report formatting changes no game behaviour but re-introduces the 'continuously patching' pattern this round is meant to stop.

candidates.name: 3.6.2-E.1 diagnosePlayUiRejection + ExceptionHandler null guard + build provenance
candidates.evidence: Rejection-reason logging and build-identity instrumentation; no new SDK mapping.
candidates.reason: Diagnostics/build-provenance only. diagnosePlayUiRejection exists to explain a rejection produced by isValidVirtualCall, which is not ported. Spec forbids mixing diagnostics with SDK functional changes.

candidates.name: Full mapping trust state machine (the dependency root)
candidates.evidence: Large refit with offline scanner parity and PE range rules.
candidates.reason: This is the ONLY way to make Batch-1/2/3 mapping hunks behave as designed, but it is a 10+ file change that also rewrites src/Solstice.cpp startup/DEBUG manual-allow and ExceptionHandler, i.e. exactly the broad non-SDK surface 3.7 forbids auto-porting. It also changes the mapping judgement rules ('do not modify mapping criteria' was a standing constraint). Presented as an explicit decision, never applied silently.
candidates.regressionRisk: HIGH - would effectively recreate the post-b32d185 change surface
optionsForUser: A: keep S1 deferred; accept b32d185's original mappings and ship only S2 (lowest risk, recommended for STABLE_BASELINE_RESTORED)
B: authorise a separate, isolated state-machine batch with its own S-stage and validation, explicitly accepting the Solstice.cpp/ExceptionHandler changes
